topStories.headline: Four Days Out: The D8 Supervisor Race Narrows to Three as Election Day Arrives
topStories.dek: With voting on November 3, the race to replace term-limited Supervisor Rafael Mandelman has consolidated around Gary McCoy, Darshini Patel, and Michael Nguyen after Manny Yekutiel's early-October exit.
topStories.body:
San Francisco's District 8 supervisor race — covering the Castro, Noe Valley, Glen Park, Diamond Heights and surrounding neighborhoods — reaches its conclusion on November 3 with three candidates on the effective ballot. Manny Yekutiel, who had been a prominent contender, suspended his campaign on October 1 following multiple sexual-assault allegations, which he denied. Because ballots had already been finalized when he withdrew, his name still appears in the voting booth.

The three active candidates are Gary McCoy, a former political director for Rep. Nancy Pelosi; Darshini Patel, a community advocate and former White House staffer; and Michael Nguyen, a patent attorney. All three have centered their campaigns on housing affordability — a particularly acute issue in a district where Castro Merchants have counted 68 vacant storefronts in the Castro alone and where District 8 has completed only sixteen new homes so far this year.

Endorsements have reshuffled significantly since Yekutiel's exit. State Sen. Scott Wiener and several sitting supervisors moved to support McCoy, while advocacy group GrowSF endorsed Patel as its first choice, noting that McCoy's updated public-safety platform had moved him closer to alignment. Nguyen has drawn backing from Our Revolution, UESF, and the Solidarity Club SF. Former Yekutiel accuser Brad Chapin publicly endorsed Patel.

Voters in these neighborhoods are choosing their representative using ranked-choice voting. Polls close November 3 at 8 p.m.

topStories.headline: Noe Valley Burglary Suspect Charged With 10 Counts After Pre-Dawn Break-In Spree
topStories.dek: Levi Michael Banks, 38, faces ten charges after prosecutors say he carried out a string of hot-prowl burglaries on Noe Valley residential blocks beginning in September.
topStories.body:
A San Francisco man was charged this week with ten counts of burglary after prosecutors say he broke into occupied homes across Noe Valley, Pacific Heights, and Presidio Heights in a weeks-long hot-prowl spree. Levi Michael Banks, 38, was taken into custody after police linked a backpack containing cash, identification documents, and stolen clothing to the alleged crimes.

Prosecutors say the reported break-ins in Noe Valley hit the 4100 and 4200 blocks of 24th Street, the 600 block of Elizabeth Street, and the 900 block of Noe Street. The earliest known incident struck Noe Valley in September, and the string of break-ins continued into October before Banks was arrested. The case was reported by Hoodline and SFist on October 29, 2026.

Hot-prowl burglaries — in which residents are present in the home during the break-in — are considered more serious than standard property crimes and are not routinely tracked as a separate category in citywide statistics. The charges follow a period in which neighborhood residents on Nextdoor and community platforms had flagged late-night intrusions in the 24th and Church Street area.

topStories.headline: Castro Station's Long-Awaited Elevator Was Targeting a Fall 2026 Opening — Here's Where It Stands
topStories.dek: More than three years after construction began on the $11.5 million glass elevator at Harvey Milk Plaza, the structure is complete and has been awaiting state certification for public use.
topStories.body:
The new glass elevator at Castro Muni Station at Harvey Milk Plaza was projected by SFMTA to be completed in Fall 2026, according to the project page — but as of late October, no ribbon-cutting date has been publicly announced. Construction began in June 2023, and the four-stop elevator has faced repeated schedule slippages: an early-2026 target gave way to a July ribbon-cutting announcement in June, which in turn was pushed to an early-fall window after state inspectors had yet to certify the elevator for public use.

As of early August, the Bay Area Reporter reported that the physical elevator tower was complete, but that state inspectors still needed to sign off on safety before SFMTA could open it to riders. SFMTA told the Castro Merchants Association at its August meeting that it hoped to receive state clearance by September and open the elevator by late September or early October — a window that has now passed without a public announcement of an opening.

The elevator will serve four levels: the underground inbound platform, the station concourse, Harvey Milk Plaza itself, and a new street-level stop at Market Street that will allow riders from the 35 and 37 bus lines to enter directly. The project also widened the surrounding sidewalk, replaced plaza lighting, and regraded pavement to improve accessibility. The elevator is required to bring the station into full Americans with Disabilities Act compliance. A separate, larger redesign of Harvey Milk Plaza — funded in part by a $25 million allocation from Proposition B — is expected to break ground in 2027 and open in 2028.

events.title: Halloween in the Castro: Block Party & Night Market
events.location: 18th Street between Diamond and Noe, Castro
events.description: Four blocks and three stages of free Halloween fun presented by CG Events, the Castro Merchants Association, and the Civic Joy Fund. Festivities include trick-or-treating, a costume contest, live entertainment, food vendors, and a neon glow dance party.

events.title: Haunted Chenery — Glen Park's Car-Free Halloween
events.location: Chenery Street between Diamond and Elk, Glen Park
events.description: The Glen Park Association closes Chenery Street to traffic for its annual neighborhood trick-or-treat tradition, drawing thousands of costumed revelers. This year features 175 carved pumpkins — including 35 organic ones carved in the days leading up to Halloween — and a Trunk or Treat at St. John Catholic School at 925 Chenery.

events.title: Castro Art Mart — First Sunday
events.location: Noe Street at Market Street, Castro
events.description: The monthly Castro Art Mart mini block party returns with LGBTQ artists, live music, and drag performances on Noe Street next to the Lookout Bar. Free and family-friendly, hosted by Castro Merchants.

events.title: Castro Art Walk — November Edition
events.description: The monthly self-guided Castro Art Walk invites neighbors to visit local businesses hosting special art events throughout the neighborhood. Free to attend; organized by the Castro Merchants Association.

events.title: Noe Valley Night Market
events.location: Noe Valley Town Square, 24th Street, Noe Valley
events.description: A free monthly evening market at the Noe Valley Town Square with live music, local retail vendors, food, and family-friendly activities. A good way to support small businesses heading into the holiday season.

moreNews.headline: Glen Park Rec Center's Small Field Closed Through November 23 for Turf Work
moreNews.body: The small field behind the Glen Park Recreation Center is temporarily closed for turf restoration from Monday, October 19 through Monday, November 23, according to the Glen Park Association's website. The closure was announced ahead of the GPA's fall quarterly meeting held October 20 at Cuppa on Diamond Street.

moreNews.headline: Permits Filed to Replace Noe Valley Victorian With New Duplex on 23rd Street
moreNews.body: A permit application filed with the city proposes demolishing a pre-1906 Victorian at 4368 23rd Street in Noe Valley and replacing it with a roughly 47-foot-tall duplex containing a four-bedroom primary residence and a one-bedroom rental unit — about 4,500 square feet total. The application was reported by Hoodline on October 12, 2026. The site sits near the 24th Street commercial corridor. No demolition or construction date has been set.
